title: Apollo 11 - CSM Columbia

call_signs._comment: The call signs CAPCOM uses for the flight and its vehicles (Mission.words(): {mission}, {csm}, {lm}, {lm_landed} in the calls) [published]

start_calls.launch: T minus 20 seconds and counting. We are still GO with {mission}.
start_calls.translunar_coast: {csm}, Houston. Good trajectory. Request an MCC PAD when you are ready; LOI PAD about eight hours out.
start_calls.lunar_orbit: {csm}, Houston. You are in a 54 by 66-mile orbit with {lm} docked. LM JETT, then request the TEI PAD.
start_calls.lunar_descent: {lm}, Houston. You're on the descent orbit. Your state vector and GO for PDI are coming.
start_calls.lunar_surface: {lm_landed}, Houston. You're STAY. The ascent PAD comes at {ascent_pad}.
start_calls.lunar_ascent: {lm}, Houston. Your ascent PAD is in: liftoff at {liftoff}. P12 when you're ready.
start_calls.tei: {csm}, Houston. The LM is gone, and your TEI PAD is on its way up.
start_calls.transearth_coast: Houston: TEI was good. Request MCC PADs to put you in the entry corridor.
start_calls.entry: Houston: entry interface in about twenty minutes. P61, CM/SM SEP when P62 asks, ELS LOGIC and AUTO.
start_calls._comment: CAPCOM's word as each start phase begins, the simulator's own [adapted]: {ascent_pad} is the ascent PAD's GET and {liftoff} the liftoff's

_comment: Mission profile. Timeline values are Apollo 11 figures rounded [published]. The Moon and the Sun are JPL's for the mission's dates (moon.ephemeris, from tools/ephemeris/fit_ephemeris.py); a moon block of inclination_deg, raan_deg, phase0_deg and sun_phase_deg flies the circular model instead. Distances in km, times in GET seconds.

launch._comment: Apollo 11's launch from Launch Complex 39A (NASA KSC's coordinates, taken as geocentric on the simulator's round Earth [simplified]) at 13:32:00 UTC, GET 0 [published]. The start phase begins on the pad at start_get_s: guidance reference release at grr_get_s, the S-IC's start sequence commanded at ignition_get_s and its five engines at thrust by thrust_ok_get_s (Table 2-2) [published]. The Instrument Unit's boost program on its time bases as AS-506 flew it (flight evaluation report, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, Table 2-2) [published]: T1 at the umbilical disconnect; the S-IC's centre engine cutoff on it; T2 there, the tilt arrest on it; T3 at the S-IC's outboard engines' cutoff, which the propellant ends, then staging, the S-II's start, the aft interstage's and the launch escape tower's jettison, the iterative guidance's start, the S-II's centre engine cutoff and the mixture ratio's shift; T4 at the S-II's cutoff, which its propellant ends, then staging and the S-IVB's ignition; T5 at the S-IVB's velocity cutoff, and insertion after it. The yaw away from the tower, the tilt's start (at 137 m, or T1 13 s), the attitude rate limit and the time-tilt pitch polynomial (degrees from the launch vertical, in T1 seconds, by segment) are SA-504's presettings (Saturn V Launch Vehicle Guidance Equations, SA-504, Boeing D5-15706-4, Table 5-1) [published; estimated for AS-506, whose presettings aren't at hand], in the pitch plane of the flight azimuth fixed at guidance reference release. The S-IVB loses parking_orbit_loss_kg of propellant, vented and burned, between its first cutoff and its second start (Table 20-9) [published]: the simulator takes it off at insertion [simplified]

launch_aborts._comment: Apollo 11's launch abort modes (Apollo 11 Mission Operation Report, M-932-69-11, pp. 55 to 57; CSM Apollo Operations Handbook, SM2A-03-BLOCK II-(1), section 2.9) [published unless marked]. Mode I, the launch escape tower's, from the liftoff to the tower's jettison: IA with the pitch control motor for the first 42 s, IB with the canards, IC from about 100,000 ft, which Houston marked at 1:58; mode I lands between the launch site and 520 nmi downrange. Mode II, from the tower's jettison: the CSM separates from the launch vehicle and the CM from the SM, and the CM falls to a full-lift entry on the ground track 440 to 3,200 nmi downrange. Mode III, from when the full-lift landing reaches 3,200 nmi, near the S-II's cutoff (iii_get_s) [derived]: the SPS burns retrograde so that the half-lift entry lands no farther than 3,350 nmi downrange, about 70 nmi south of the ground track, 3,000 to 3,350 nmi out; the ground aims just inside the area's far edge, at mode_iii_target_nmi, for as small a burn as will do [estimated]. Mode IV, from 9:00 (Houston's mark; about 8:30 in the report): the SPS takes the CSM into orbit, Apollo 11's alternate mission 1 (press kit); the ground prefers it to modes II and III unless the crew must come home at once. The S-IVB could stage early and reach orbit from 5:27 (coi_get_s) [simplified: the simulator aborts instead]. The calls are the flight's (Apollo 11 Flight Journal): Armstrong's One Bravo at 0:44, and Houston's. Half lift is the lift rolled 60 degrees, cos 60 being a half [derived]; the ground's mode III and IV ignitions are mode_iii_tig_s and mode_iv_tig_s after the CSM's separation [estimated]: for mode III, time for the crew to turn the CSM retrograde on the SCS at RATE HIGH (7 deg/s) and select P40, for the CSM falls fast; for mode IV, for the CMC's own auto maneuver at 1 deg/s

parking_orbit._comment: Apollo 11's orbit at insertion, from the Saturn V flight evaluation report for AS-506 (Table 4-5): inclination 32.521 deg and descending node 123.088 deg east of the launch meridian at liftoff, insertion at 32.672 N 52.694 W, 191.1 km [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The report's 186.0 x 183.2 km orbit is taken as circular [simplified]

launch_refsmmat._comment: The launch pad REFSMMAT, the orientation the CMC's IMU was released at liftoff: X horizontal along the flight azimuth (72.058 deg, the flight evaluation report's), Z down along Launch Complex 39A's vertical, Y = Z x X, each a stable member axis in the ICRF, from tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The parking_orbit and translunar_coast start phases start aligned to it

tli._comment: TLI's conic, as the flown TLI left the stack on it: C3 -1,391,607 m2/s2 and eccentricity 0.97696, in the plane of inclination 31.383 deg and descending node 121.847 deg (AS-506 flight evaluation report, MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, Table 10-6: the postflight trajectory at TLI, 10 s after the cutoff signal, the J-2's thrust decay having added 4 m/s to the C3 of -1,487,528 at the signal, Table 4-2) [published]; the plane in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. C3 is the two-body V2 - 2mu/R (ibid.), as Sivb.energy_of() reckons it. The RTCC plans TLI's ignition time and energy (Rtcc.plan_tli()) for the free return the flown TLI left the stack on, past the Moon 896.3 nmi up at 75:05:21, where the preflight plan had 718.9 nmi (Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, Table 7-III and section 7.4.1) [published], keeping the conic's plane and perigee; its energy comes out within the metre a second the report's trajectory solutions spread (ibid., section 4.3.4). The midcourse correction then aims at pericynthion_alt_km over the landing site, at pericynthion_get, where Apollo 11's first left it (61.5 nmi at 75:53:35, ibid., Table 7-III) [published]

loi._comment: LOI-1's targets: Apollo 11's 170 by 60 nmi ellipse (flown 169.7 by 60.0 nmi above the landing site's radius: MSC-00171, Table 7-V) [published], taken above the Moon's mean radius [simplified]

lunar_orbit._comment: Apollo 11's lunar orbit after LOI-2, above the landing site's radius (the mission report's datum): targeted 65.7 by 53.7 nmi, noncircular, for the Moon's field to round it toward 60 nmi by the rendezvous (the RTCC's R2 model said 59.9 by 59.3 at 126 h; the orbit was 62.4 by 56.6), and achieved 65.7 by 53.8 with its pericynthion at about 80 deg W, LOI-2 cutting off at 80:11:54 [published: Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, sections 7.4.4 and 7.7]. The lunar_orbit start phase starts there, on the flown timeline; LOI-2's PAD targets it

tei._comment: TEI onto Apollo 11's return: the flown TEI came to 1,000.8 m/s (3,283.6 ft/s) at 135:23:41.56 (the TEI-30 PAD, Apollo Flight Journal 134:01:16) [published], its N81 +3,201.1, +681.8, -265.0 ft/s, from which the RTCC starts its solve, and entry interface came at 195:03:05.7, 3.19 deg S 171.96 deg E, heading 50.18 deg east of north (MSC-00171, Table 7-VII) [published]: a return inclined 39.9 deg to the equator, cos i = cos(latitude) sin(heading) [derived]. The RTCC solves the burn at the flown TEI's time for that inclination, that entry interface and the corridor's vacuum perigee (Rtcc.plan_tei())

entry._comment: Apollo 11's target, N61 in the final entry PAD at 191:43:57 (Apollo Flight Journal) [published]: 13.32 deg N, 169.17 deg W, some 1,500 nmi from entry interface, where the weather moved it from the planned 1,285 nmi (the TEI PAD's N61, 11.03 deg N, 172.37 deg W). The ground uplinks it with the entry PAD (the lunar timeline's entry_pad), and the entry start phase starts with it loaded

doi._comment: Descent orbit insertion: the LM's pericynthion at 50,000 ft [published], where powered descent begins, on the pass that lands at the landing time

landing._comment: Apollo 11's landing site and landing time, 102:45:40 GET [published]. The site's height is the terrain's there (data/terrain/). The lunar_surface and lunar_ascent start phases leave the descent stage the propellant the simulator's automatic landing leaves (tests/scenarios/test_landing.gd) [estimated]

pdi._comment: The LM state vector the ground uplinks with the PDI PAD is off by this much at PDI, in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down): the LGC thinks Eagle is 250 m farther along, 150 m to the right and 900 m higher [estimated]
pdi._aborts: Slice 9e. The PDI PAD's abort TPIs, as seconds after its TIG (102:33:04.36): for an abort less than 10 minutes after PDI, TPI at 105:12:30.00; for one after, TPI at 107:11:30.00 [published: Apollo 11 Flight Journal, day 5, part 2, the PAD read at 100:22:05]. Apollo 11's later aborts also had a phasing burn at 103:40:00 (ibid.); here CSI at the first apolune sets the coelliptic height that brings TPI then [simplified]

lgc._p52: Eagle's IMU (slice 11a): its gyros' drift, +4.5, -5.0 and +0.4 mERU, from the torquing of the P57 at 103:47 against the P52 after undocking (Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, Table 9.6-I) [published]; that P52, on stars 25 (Acrux, in the front detent) and 33 (Antares), its star angle difference 0.03 deg and its N93 -0.292, +0.289 and -0.094 deg, which Armstrong read out at 101:19:46 and torqued at 101:20:18 (ibid., which lists it at 100:15; the Apollo Flight Journal, 101:17:07 to 101:20:18) [published]. The sequencer takes the platform at undocking to be where that P52 found it, less the drift between (_lgc_undocked())
lgc._comment: Eagle's LGC program [published]. Luminary 1A counted the rendezvous radar CDUs' pulses while the radar's mode switch was away from LGC, which brought the 1202 and 1201 alarms of the landing; Luminary 1B, flown from Apollo 12, zeroed the CDUs (Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, section 16.2) [published]. The other missions leave this out: their LGCs zero them

ascent._comment: The RTCC times the liftoff for the CSM to lead the LM by this angle at insertion: the lead that, flying Apollo 11's coelliptic sequence (CSI at the first apolune, circularizing 15 nmi below the CSM; TPI at 26.6 deg elevation), puts TPI where it was flown, 2 h 35 min after insertion (124:29:17 to 127:03:52 GET [published]) [estimated]

rendezvous._comment: The coelliptic sequence: CSI at the LM's first apolune; TPI 2 h 35 min after insertion, as Apollo 11 flew it (124:29:17 to 127:03:52 GET), and the midcourse corrections 15 and 30 min after TPI (Apollo 11: 14 min 39 s and 29 min 39 s) [published]. The CSM state vector the ground uplinks with the CSI PAD is off by MSFN's tracking error, LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down) [estimated]; the rendezvous radar's marks take it out

dispersions._comment: The seed the flight's dispersions are drawn from: the CSM's unmodelled forces (spacecraft.json "unmodelled"), once for the flight, and MSFN's tracking error ("msfn"), for each uplink. A checkpoint carries the forces and where the draws have got to

msfn._comment: The Manned Space Flight Network's tracking error in the CSM state vector the RTCC plans the CSM's PADs from and uplinks with them (P27): standard deviations in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down), by the body the CSM's orbit is about [estimated]

timeline._comment: Mission Control from undocking to the entry. Each entry happens once: at its GET ('get'), or 's' seconds 'after' a mission event or 'before' a time the ground has planned (doi_tig, pdi_tig, liftoff_tig, csi_tig, tei_tig), if its condition ('when') holds then; CAPCOM makes the call ('say') and the ground uplinks the PAD ('pad'). A PAD with 'near' takes the opportunity nearest that GET, and none is uplinked while the last of its kind is still to be flown. The DOI PAD follows an undocking within 6 h of the landing time. The times and calls are Apollo 11's [published: the Apollo 11 Flight and Lunar Surface Journals: undocking 100:12:03, DOI PAD 100:20:32, GO for DOI 101:17:53 with DOI at 101:36:14, GO for powered descent 102:28:08 with PDI at 102:33:05, touchdown 102:45:40, STAY for T2 102:51:45 and T3 104:21:16, liftoff 124:22:00, GO for CSI 125:06:47 with CSI at 125:19:35, docking 128:03:00, GO for jettison 130:07:49, TEI PADs 134:01:16, TEI 135:23:42, the final entry PAD 191:43:57], except the entries marked estimated. The LM start phases undock at 'undocking_get'

entries.say: Eagle, Houston. You're GO for undocking.
Eagle, Houston. You are GO for DOI.
Eagle, Houston. If you read, you're GO for powered descent.
Tranquility Base, Houston. You are STAY for T2.
Tranquility Base, Houston. You are STAY for T3.

entries._estimated: the PAD's time, two hours before the liftoff

entries._published: the crew's last P57 before the liftoff, at 123:49, option 4, to the landing site at the liftoff's time (Apollo 11 Mission Report, MSC-00171, Table 9.6-I); simplified: until slice 11b's P57, made for them, exactly

entries.say: Eagle, Houston. You're cleared for takeoff.
Eagle, Houston. We're GO for CSI.
Columbia, Houston. You're GO for jettison.
